capacity_source: The service's own daily reservoir report where it publishes a full level (ADR-070), the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers National Inventory of Dams otherwise, with named reviewed corrections
selection: Reservoir-storage stations reporting within the last year, inside the western drainage scope, not already represented by provider point, reviewed dam point or name, with a confirmed dam and no unresolved disagreement between sources -- and the named reviewed admissions below, each carrying the screen it was admitted against

withheld.HVS: Lake Havasu. Parker Dam's reviewed full level is 646,200 acre-feet (Bureau of Reclamation, https://www.usbr.gov/projects/index.php?id=207, checked 2026-08-20), against the inventory's 180,000. Held anyway: the series carries two readings near 5,913,000 acre-feet against a third highest of 601,300, roughly ten times the reservoir, and a reading this project cannot explain is not repaired.
withheld.ONF: O'Neill Forebay, matched to B.F. Sisk Dam 1.18 km away and carrying San Luis Reservoir's 2,094,900 acre-feet -- thirty-seven times its own, reading 21% full at its fullest. The dam identity belongs to San Luis, which is admitted above.
withheld.FMT: Fairmont. The inventory's 7,507 acre-feet against a regulating forebay its operator describes at about 500; the 423 acre-feet seen is the reservoir full, not 6% of it.
withheld.VIL: Vail Lake. Its own sources disagree by 19% about the denominator -- 42,680 acre-feet in Rancho California Water District material against the inventory's 51,000 -- and the district's record is not in this pipeline. A reviewed figure would settle it.
withheld.BMP: Bon Tempe. Five usable readings ever, the last in March 2023. Screened out by the audit's own recency rule rather than held here; named because it was publishable before that rule.
withheld.GDR: Guadalupe Reservoir. Held for a series whose highest reading is 1,762 acre-feet against a third highest of 402, and quiet since December 2021 besides.

review.why: A real reservoir that has simply been low every year since 2015. Two sources agree on the denominator within 1% -- the inventory's 50,206 acre-feet against the City of San Diego's 50,694 -- so 28% is a measurement.

A flood-control dam operated empty on purpose. Martis Creek has never been seen above 5% of its pool and never will be; the percentage is true and useless, which is a fact about the reservoir rather than about the denominator.
